newsitem.title: UK: Sheep dips poison British river life-ecologists.
newsitem.headline: Sheep dips poison British river life-ecologists.

text.p: New and much more toxic pesticides used in sheep dips are damaging British rivers and killing off mayflies and freshwater shrimps, ecologists said on Thursday.
They said a new breed of pesticides known as synthetic pyrethroids were 100 times more toxic than those used before.

"We have probably had as many cases of pollution from sheep dip in the past year as in the previous 10 years," Donny Morrison of the Scottish Environmental Protection Agency told the New Scientist weekly on Thursday.
He said farmers had become careless about disposing of the dip, which is used to protect the animals from sheep scab, skin mites and lice.
The report said the pesticides were stealthy killers. Sheep who dripped any of the pesticide while grazing near a stream could kill freshwater shrimps with just a few drops.
